notes.title: Exported Maps Split, Discord Link, Bug Fixes
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Previously, exported maps for terrain, temperature, and rainfall, had their values separated into the four colour channels (RBGA). This was difficult to work with for many users, so now all these maps are separated into greyscale maps and named accordingly.
[*] Added a link to the Discord server
[*] Fixed bug causing crust "implosion" (crust would disappear everywhere except at the plate boundaries)
[*] Fixed spurious continental crust appearing seemingly randomly inside oceanic crust
[*] Tuned down continental crust creation in general
[*] Fixed a bug that caused continental crust to subduct beneath oceanic crust in circumstances where it shouldn't
[*] Fixed a bug causing divergent boundaries to meander/drift too aggressively
[/list]

notes.title: Tectonics
notes.content:
The Tectonics update is now live, and represents a massive step forward for world generation tools. 

[b]Everything has changed. [/b]

[h1]New workflow[/h1]
The new workflow is all about the simulations. The simulations are run by specifying a geological/eroded age with the Megaannum sliders in the Tectonics and Erosion tabs. You can click/drag on the slider to set a specific age or use the buttons to the left and right to watch the history of the planet unfold, pause it at any point, or reset the simulation.

You can always re-run either simulation, but each run will be different as they are not 100% deterministic simulations and small random changes build up and cascade into large differences over these timescales. So even with the same seed, just re-running the simulations can give entirely different geographies.
 
While the simulations are running you can swap between any of the visualisations or projections, and most of the parameters can be changed to have their effects immediately applied to the simulation going forward. Some parameters are marked [b]<< like this >>[/b] and these will reset the simulation if altered. 

[h2]Tectonics simulation[/h2]
After you've set up your quality and initial conditions, start the tectonics simulation by setting a Megannum age. I find it usually takes a few hundred Ma before it starts to really look good. Play around with the interactions between gravity, erosion, rigidity, and to get creative with continent shapes and mountain ranges. 

[h2]Erosion simulation[/h2]
Once you've stopped the tectonics simulation, you can run the erosion simulation, which carves mountains and coastlines with hydraulic, thermal, and tidal erosion. The effects build up slowly but become noticeable around 25Ma and I find the sweet spot to be about 50-60Ma. 

[h2]Climate modelling[/h2]
Climate is simplified to the physical processes of insolation, greenhouse, and rainfall, and runs alongside the simulations. However this comes at a performance cost so if you're noticing a framerate hit, switch to the Elevation or Magma/Sedimentation visualisation -- where the climate modelling is paused until the simulation ends or you switch to another visualisation.

[i]PS. The next major update will be a realtime atmospheric climate simulation.[/i]

[h1]New UI[/h1]
[list]
[*]Hovering the mouse over the planet shows a detailed breakdown of the surface 
[*]Hovering the mouse over a button or parameter shows a tooltip explaining what it does
[*]Many parameters now map to physical properties
[*]Hints for how to control the camera with the mouse are available in the top left by hovering the mouse over them
[/list]
[h3]Known issues[/h3]
As far as I could I've attempted to address all bugs and issues, but I'm aware of two which I still haven't gotten to the bottom of. 
[list]
[*]Sometimes the tectonics simulation will randomly just "implode", and all crust will disappear except the newest crust at plate boundaries. This can be fixed by changing the seed or quality but when it happens it is annoying
[*]Sometimes when starting the tectonics simulation the app will hang for a bit before it starts
[/list]

notes.title: Incoming Tectonics Update
notes.content:
[h1]A major step forward in realistic world generation[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41923122/4e80d2912d244fbf24231f580f797271c7d7c231.jpg[/img]

The new tectonics and erosion simulations work together to create believable and detailed environments, perfect for creators who want their worlds to feel authentic and scientifically grounded. 

[h2]Incoming Major Changes[/h2]

[h3]Advanced Tectonic Simulation[/h3]
[list]
[*]Realistic plate tectonics for up to 5 billion years of simulation
[*]Mountains and continental crust forms naturally through plate collisions and subduction orogeny
[*]Organic supercontinent cycles and continental/oceanic equilibrium
[/list]
[h3]Comprehensive Erosion System[/h3]
[list]
[*]Realistic water flow and sediment transport
[*]Hydraulic and thermal weathering with variable rock hardness
[*]Temperature-dependent glacial erosion
[/list]
[h3]Updated Climate Modeling[/h3]
[list]
[*]Köppen–Geiger climate classification
[*]Complete seasonal weather patterns
[*]Realistic ocean currents and heat transport
[/list]
[h3]Worlds[/h3]
[list]
[*]Maximum quality/resolution of worlds massively increased (up to 4.95 million cells), scaling with GPU RAM
[*]Output map resolution increased to 8K (or maximum resolution supported by GPU)
[*]Galaxies are now realistic instead of stylized
[/list]
[h3]UI improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*]Most sliders now have values with units mapping to real physical properties
[*]Tooltips added to explain what toggles and sliders do (tooltips appear in bottom left when mouse is over options)
[*]Mouse controls explained (hover over icons in top left)
[/list]

[i][b]This update is not compatible with existing Rock3 worlds, and will no longer support the existing simplified instantaneous workflow.[/b][/i]

I am aiming to release this update as soon as possible, ideally within the next week or two. The only thing remaining is testing and tuning for AMD GPUs and older machines.

notes.title: Cycles Update
notes.content:
Rock 3 now models daily, yearly, and long term periodic orbital variations and the impact on climates. This paves the way for more accurate Koppen biome modelling, and gives the ability to customize worlds even further. 

Beyond that, several other quality of life improvements and feature requests have been incorporated, alongside some aesthetic ones too. 

First up, now every planet generates its own unique galaxy. I plan to expand on this to increase variety in future updates. 
[previewyoutube=qEKIf9Hj7Bc;full][/previewyoutube]

Mouse controls have been re-worked for consistency. Now, the left mouse button controls the time of day in globe and map views, the middle button controls camera rotation in globe and projection orientation in map view, and the right mouse button controls orbital position around the sun in globe and map views. 
[previewyoutube=Q6QNC321BA8;full][/previewyoutube]

When you enter the map projection view, or toggle off the atmospheric effects, you now enter a new focused visualization mode making it easier to see details.
[previewyoutube=BAM4xCeCE3A;full][/previewyoutube]

The day/night cycle is now visible on the map projection view, which I personally found to really clarify how strongly seasonal changes correlate with the length of days near the poles. 
[previewyoutube=BQkfWQTcPts;full][/previewyoutube]

You can now toggle latitude and longitude grid lines in all views, to make it easier to see variations in tilt and rotation through the cycles.
[previewyoutube=Ajyr4DhY2DI;full][/previewyoutube]

For example, grid lines make it much easier to see how Milankovitch cycles affect the planet's rotation axis.
[previewyoutube=6Q21Hv266T4;full][/previewyoutube]

Finally, when you slow a planet's rotation speed right now, you can create tidally locked or near-locked planets, which concentrates heat strongly towards the side facing the sun. 
[previewyoutube=asQ02QllEIo;full][/previewyoutube]

I hope this update helps you create more interesting and creative worlds! Please stay tuned for future updates, such as the upcoming overhaul of tectonic plates for more realistic continents, moving to Koppen biome modelling, and UI enhancements to provide detailed breakdowns of surface statistics.

notes.title: First update: Fixes and improvements
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41923122/f667c4a665ac7c337207dea0d12bb95b7c9e2566.jpg[/img]
It was a lot more challenging than I'd ever imagined, but I've finally resolved the AMD rendering issues. To maintain my sanity while troubleshooting, I've also implemented a range of enhancements and feature requests, such as: 
[list]
[*] Greyscale heightmaps now exported alongside the other maps
[*] Rotate the sun around the planet while holding the right mouse button
[*] Zoom in/out with the mouse wheel
[*] Added lens flare and bloom for sun in globe view
[*] Adjusted rainfall to give more realistic biome distributions
[*] Several performance improvements
[/list]
A few of the items coming in the next update: 
[list]
[*] A new tectonics model for more realistic continents and islands
[*] Climate cycles (on the order of several thousand years)
[*] Swapping over to the Koppen biome model
[*] Move the mouse over the planet surface to see a breakdown of stats at that point, like elevation, temperature, rainfall, biome classification, wind direction, etc. 
[/list]
If you've been unable to use Rock 3 due to the AMD rendering issue, I appreciate your patience and I hope it was worth the wait!
